About the Role
How do you translate evolving financial crime regulations into practical, effective KYC processes?

We are looking for experienced KYC Process Specialists to support an AMLR implementation project within the banking sector. Working closely with internal process experts and project drivers, you will help translate new and updated AML/CTF regulatory requirements into detailed process changes and operational guidance.

You will play an important role in ensuring that updated KYC requirements are effectively implemented across the entire process lifecycle. The initiatives cover areas such as PEP requirements, Purpose and Nature of Relationship, customer risk scoring, adverse media screening and ongoing due diligence.

Key Responsibilities
• 
Work closely with internal process experts and project drivers to operationalise AMLR-related requirements.

• 
Translate external AMLR and Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS), together with updated internal AML/CTF rules, into detailed process changes.

• 
Define and document changes to KYC processes to ensure effective end-to-end implementation of the new requirements.

• 
Support the implementation of updated requirements related to Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs).

• 
Define process updates concerning Purpose and Nature of Relationship requirements.

• 
Develop procedural updates related to customer risk scoring changes.

• 
Support changes to adverse media screening processes.

• 
Implement operational changes related to Ongoing Due Diligence (ODD) cycle requirements.

• 
Develop clear instructions and guidance for operational staff.

• 
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to ensure consistent operationalisation of regulatory requirements.

Qualifications and ExperienceMust-Have Requirements
• 
Strong knowledge of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter-Terrorist Financing (CTF).

• 
Good understanding of Know Your Customer (KYC) processes.

• 
Experience working with KYC, Financial Crime or business process development and change initiatives.

• 
Strong analytical skills and the ability to assess complex requirements.

• 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

• 
CV must be submitted in English.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications
• 
Legal background or relevant legal knowledge.

• 
Ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical operational processes.

• 
Ability to explain complex regulatory matters clearly and simply.

• 
Knowledge of Ongoing Due Diligence (ODD) requirements.

• 
Familiarity with PEP requirements, Purpose and Nature of Relationship, adverse media screening and customer risk scoring.

jobs.occupation: Engineer 50 % temporary position linked to AQUAPHAGE
jobs.description:
The position
We have a 50% temporary position available as a departmental engineer. The position is linked to the “Optimising Phage Performance in Mucosal Conditions for Moritella viscosa Prevention – AQUAPHAGE” project funded by MABIT. 

AQUAPHAGE is an innovation-based project connecting the Marine Bioprospecting group of the BFE-NFH-UiT (within the CANS II network) and the ACD Pharma AS company located in Leknes, Norway. It benefits from the ACD Pharma phage collection and the expertise of the research group with the Bacteriophage Adherence to Mucus (BAM) model. 

AQUAPHAGE summary: 

Winter ulcers associated with Moritella viscosa are one of the most important health problems for salmon farming in Norway. Vaccination is not sufficient to protect fish farms from outbreaks, while antibiotic treatments are strictly regulated and pose a risk for antimicrobial resistance selection. Phage therapy, the use of viruses of bacteria to treat bacterial infections, is a proven medical method with enormous potential for aquaculture applications. One advantage in aquaculture is that some phages have evolved to be more effective on mucosal surfaces, naturally serving as a non-host derived immune barrier against invading bacteria. Phage-based prophylaxis based on mucosal dynamics has been shown to be an efficient method to control diseases in rainbow trout and in yellow catfish, but not in Atlantic salmon. AQUAPHAGE will combine the industrial competence of ACD Pharma and the research environment of the Norwegian College of Fishery Science of the UiT, aiming at rationally design a phage-based prophylactic approach to control M. viscosa infections. Phages from ACD Pharma will be ranked based on their adhesion and performance under mucosal conditions, their stability will be tested and desired phenotypes will be improved in vitro. At the end, it is expected that we will identify the best phage candidates for a pilot product development, representing the first phage-based solution in aquaculture to consider mucosal dynamics as key factors to improve fish health. 

The position is expected to run for 12 months (start 4.1.27) and has no teaching component included.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within 6 months after receiving the offer.
Job description
Key responsibilities: 

• The candidate will be responsible for 
• assessment of phage killing efficacy in simulated mucosal conditions 
• testing of phage stability in different storage conditions
• application of adaptive phage training to improve BAM-model associated phenotypes on phages
• evaluation of phage adherence to mucin/mucus
• data management
• reporting of results to the UiT and ACD Pharma through regular meetings, participation in the kick-off and closure meetings, 
• preparation of reports and drafting of publications are also part of the responsibilities. 
Training will be provided by the project leader and by ACD Pharma staff at the beginning of the project.
Qualifications
Required qualifications:

• Master’s degree in microbiology or associated areas.
• Practical experience with biosafety level 2 laboratory work related to microbiology.
• Documented theoretical experience (dissertations, theses, papers, others) on the field of microbiology. 
Qualifications that are considered advantageous:

• PhD degree in microbiology or associated areas.
• Practical experience with marine microorganisms. 
• Practical experience in virology, especially with phages and with phage-training.
• Practical experience in phage-mucin interactions as defined by the phenotypes associated with the BAM model.
Language requirements

The applicant must have good proficiency in both written and spoken English. Proficiency in Norwegian is considered an advantage.

The assessment will emphasize the candidate’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. We are looking for candidate’s who have:

• Good collaboration skills
• Abilities for good communication and interaction with colleagues and partners
• Abilities and desires to contribute to a good working environmentWe offer
• A good working environment with dedicated colleagues
• Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement
• Pension scheme through the state pension fund
The remuneration for the position is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1085 avdelingsingeniør with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 505 000 to 620 000 (in a 100% position) or code 1087 overingeniør with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 505 000 to 620 000 (in a 100% position) Depending on qualifications, with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 525 000 to 650 000 (in a 100% position). In special cases, a higher salary may be considered. There is a 2% deduction for contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund. As a state employee, you have one of the best pension schemes available. For more information see: spk.no.
Application
The application must be submitted electronically via www.jobbnorge.no, and shall include:

• CV and application letter
• Diplomas and transcripts
• Contact information to 2-3 references
All documentation has to be in English or a Scandinavian language.
Inclusion and diversity
UiT The Arctic University i Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity is a strength and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.
 
If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.
General information
The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants.

Employees who have been temporarily employed at UiT continuously for more than three years shall be deemed to be permanently employed, cf. the Civil Service Act § 9 (3).
 
A good work environment is characterized by diversity. We encourage qualified candidates to apply, regardless of their gender, functional capacity or cultural background.

UiT will emphasize making the necessary adaptations to the working conditions for employees with reduced functional ability. Questions can be directed to the contact person for the position.

jobs.description:

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network UNCHANGE, collaborate with academic, museums, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on cultural heritage science.

As part of the UNCHANGE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027, and the Head of unit will be the immediate supervisor for employment-related matters.
About the project
About the UNCHANGE project  

UNCHANGE (UNderstanding change in Cultural HeritAge: the Next Generation of Experts) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network that brings together leading European universities, research institutions, and industry partners to train the next generation of heritage scientists. The project focuses on understanding, documenting, and monitoring change in cultural heritage using advanced technologies, including imaging, materials analysis, artificial intelligence, and data science. Through an interdisciplinary and international research environment, UNCHANGE equips doctoral candidates with the skills needed to address current and future challenges in cultural heritage conservation and preservation.

About the specific Doctoral projectObjectives: (1) Investigate novel object representations, such as Gaussians and Ray Fields, in measuring change for CH objects. (2) Investigate novel object representations in capturing and visualizing CH objects. The above objectives reflect current trends in the development of new object representations that are ‘AI-Friendly’, given the pervasiveness of AI methods in all types of processing.Expected results: Determination of the effect of machine learning-friendly object representations in capturing, visualizing and measuring change on CH objects.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the Visual Computing research group.
• Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the UNCHANGE partner institutions and contribute to UNCHANGE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to NTNU Museum (Trondheim) and Peggy Guggenheim Collection, Venezia.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, imaging science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• You must have experience in Visual Computing, Machine Learning, excellent programming skills and a desire to apply your skills to Cultural Heritage.
• At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.

Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance. In addition, mobility allowance and family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations.

A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• Curriculum Vitae 
• Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline, as you imagine it (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) 
• English language certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

Evaluation processApplications will be assessed by an expert committee based on the qualifications and documentation submitted by the applicants. The evaluation will consider academic achievements, the quality and relevance of the applicant's educational background, research potential, and suitability for the position. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview. The final appointment will be made in accordance with the applicable regulations for employment at the university. 
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.
